vo: Every flight starts the same way. A walk-around. A checklist. Fuel. Doors. Cargo. It's why flying works.
Software? It just takes off. Written on Tuesday. Shipped on Thursday. And nobody checks what's on board.
Until the complaint lands. Customer ID numbers. No reason. No end date. And one question. Who approved this?
Regulators are asking too. One million rand for a bank. Half a million for a college.
So let's go back to the gate. This is Preflight.
Step one. The scanner. Preflight reads every Jira ticket as it's written, and spots personal data on board. ID numbers. Health details. Children's data.
Step two. The gate. Start work too soon, and it stays closed. Three questions first. Why do you need it? What's your lawful basis? When is it deleted?
Step three. Your co-pilot. Rovo drafts the answers. A person confirms them. AI can help. It can't approve.
Step four. The control tower. Nicholas, the Information Officer, sees every waiting ticket, and clears it for take-off.
Gate open. Ben is cleared to build.
Try to sneak past? Reword the ticket. It's still flagged. Change an answer. The clearance is cancelled.
Before landing, one last check. Proof. A link to the updated privacy notice.
And everything lands in the flight recorder. Write-once. So next time someone asks, who approved this? Ten seconds.
Your airline. Your checklist. Start with POPIA or GDPR, or let Rovo draft rules from your own policy. Nothing is enforced until an approver switches it on.
Preflight. Privacy review, before you build.
